children: Nifty Metal index rose 1.5% on September 4 as traders' attention turned to key US payrolls data for clues on the Federal Reserve's next interest rate decision.
Traders are pricing in an about 50% chance of a Fed rate hike later this month, according to the CME FedWatch Tool.
The US nonfarm payrolls report is due at 6 pm IST.

The jobs report for August arrives at a time when the odds of a quarter-point Fed hike this month are roughly even. While Fed Chair Kevin Warsh last week emphasized that policymakers’ focus is firmly on inflation, employment data could help buy them time to assess whether current policy is restrictive enough to bring price pressures under control.

“The market needs a result weak enough to give the Fed a reason to keep interest rates unchanged, but not so weak that it intensifies concerns about a recession,” noted Linh Tran at XS.com. “Stronger-than-expected employment and wage growth could push yields higher again and weigh on equities.”
At 2:35 pm on September 4, Nifty Metal index was trading 1.5% higher at 13,375 with APL Apollo, Tata Steel, Hindustan Zinc leading the gains by rising 4%, 3% and 2%, respectively.

Meanwhile, Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said that recent data suggested some signs of disinflation and that, if upcoming reports reinforced that trend, he would favour holding rates steady at this month's policy meeting.

Traders are bracing for the US payrolls report for August due later in the day, although Waller did say he did not expect the data to deviate much from the current trend of a stable labour market. Forecasts are centred on a rise of 56,000 jobs after a shock fall of 23,000 the previous month. The unemployment rate is expected to hold steady at 4.1%.

title: Nifty Metal rises 1.5% ahead of US payrolls data; Tata Steel, Hindustan Zinc among top gainers
